title: Fake downloads and extensions
takeaway: Install wallets and extensions only from the official site, and check every pasted address before you send.

cards.title: The top result is a trap
cards.body: You need your wallet app on a new laptop. You search, and the top result is an ad with the right logo. The page looks perfect and asks you to import your seed phrase to finish setup.

url.label: Secure web prefix
url.why: This alone proves nothing either way.

url.why: The path is not the problem here.

page.title: Download your wallet
lines: Import your seed phrase to begin.

cards.title: Get wallets only from the source
cards.body: Install wallets and extensions only from the wallet maker's official site, or the store link that site gives you. Search ads and lookalike sites push fake copies that steal your seed phrase. Fake game launchers, meeting tools and pirated plugins can hide malware too.
points: Open the official site from your bookmark.
Skip search ads for wallet downloads.

cards.title: Even a real extension can go bad
cards.body: On 25 December 2025, Trust Wallet said version 2.68 of its browser extension had a security incident. On chain sleuth ZachXBT first estimated that over $6M was taken from hundreds of users. Users were told to disable it and update to 2.69. Keep your vault off browser extensions, and follow official accounts for alerts.

cards.title: The clipboard swap
cards.body: Some malware watches what you copy. When you copy a wallet address, it pastes the attacker's address instead. Before you send, compare the whole address on the confirm screen, not just the first and last few characters. Never paste a command that a site or helper tells you to run.
points: If it changed after pasting, stop and scan.

questions.stem: You need your wallet app on a new phone. Where do you get it?
options: The store link on the maker's official site
The top search result with the wallet's name
The app store result with the most downloads
A download link a helper sends you
questions.why: Fake wallet apps copy logos and buy ads. Start from the official site, then follow its own store link.

questions.stem: Tap the red flags in the web address, then Done.

questions.why: The domain is not the official site. A real installer never asks you to type your seed phrase on a web page.

value.label: Swapped address

questions.stem: You pasted a friend's address. On the confirm screen the middle characters differ from what you copied. What do you do?
options: Reject, your device may be swapping addresses
Send it, the start and end both match
Send a smaller test amount first
Edit the middle characters by hand
questions.why: Clipboard malware swaps copied addresses. Reject, then check the device from a clean one before sending anything.

questions.stem: A site says: verify you are human, press Win+R and paste this code. What do you do?
options: Close it, never paste commands a site gives
Paste it, it is just a check
Paste it on your phone instead
Paste it, sites use this to stop bots
questions.why: Fake verification steps that make you paste a command are a common way to install malware.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting is not the problem.

seg.label: Unasked alert
seg.why: Real wallets do not DM security alerts.

seg.label: Unofficial update site
seg.why: Updates come only from the official store.

seg.why: No update ever needs your seed phrase.

questions.why: Real updates come only through the official store or site, and no update ever needs your recovery phrase.

questions.stem: Your wallet's official account warns that one extension version is unsafe. A DM offers to help. What do you do?
options: Follow the official steps, ignore the DM
Let the DM helper guide you
Keep using it until funds move
Reinstall it from the top search result
questions.why: In the Trust Wallet case, users were told to disable and update. Follow only the official account's steps.

questions.stem: A free pirated game is shared in a server. You play on the PC that holds your wallet. What do you do?
options: Skip it, pirated software often hides malware
Install it, the server mods shared it
Install it if many people already did
Install it, then run an antivirus scan
questions.why: Fake game launchers and pirated software are known malware carriers that steal wallets.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

value.label: Swapped address
value.why: Middle differs from the address you meant.

value.label: Amount
value.why: The amount is what you typed.

questions.why: The address on screen is not the one you copied. Clipboard malware may be swapping it. Reject.

questions.stem: You paste an address. The first and last four characters match. Is that enough to send?
options: No, check the whole address
Yes, four on each end is enough
Yes, if the amount is small
Yes, if it came from history
questions.why: Scammers make addresses that match the start and end. Check well beyond the first and last four characters.

questions.stem: A free NFT sniper tool asks to read your wallet files to work faster. What do you do?
options: Skip it, tools reading wallet files steal them
Install it on your vault PC only
Install it if it is open source
Install it for one day, then remove it
questions.why: Tools that read wallet files act like infostealers. They can take seed phrases and saved logins.
